[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] QTS Data Centers, formerly QTS Realty Trust, is a large scale data center provider. Per Blackstone Real Estate Income Trusts own press release, Blackstone affiliated funds completed a roughly 10 billion dollar acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private. This specific row is one of four entries in this registry all named simply QTS in Fayette County, GA, part of this operators Fayetteville megasite. A Baxtel listing for this campus, fetched fresh this session, gives 1435 Hwy 54 W, Fayetteville, Georgia, and explicitly describes a 615 acre site planned for up to 16 buildings, DC2 through DC16, that use internal building codes rather than separate street addresses, all part of the unified Fayetteville campus. Data Center Dynamics trade press separately corroborates a 250 megawatt mega-project at this same site. Given the operators own building numbering does not carry distinct street addresses, this session applied the one confirmed campus address to all four rows rather than guessing at which specific building each represents.

reading.body:
QTS's Fayetteville campus sits on 600 acres in Fayette County, Georgia, with a planned capacity of 250 MW across up to 16 buildings designated internally as DC2 through DC16. Trade press and city sources document this as a multi-building megasite rather than a single facility, though the operator's published specifications do not confirm operating capacity for individual buildings or the campus as a whole. The planned 1.5 million square feet at full build-out suggests a campus capable of hosting a significant volume of computing infrastructure, but current delivered capacity versus construction phase remains unpublished.

At the industry assumption of 40 kW per rack for AI training workloads, a fully built 250 MW campus would accommodate roughly 6,250 racks, though this figure is planned capacity, not confirmed operating capacity. Georgia has published capacity of 66.3 MW across four facilities with disclosed figures, placing this campus at rank 5 in the state by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects only confirmed operating figures, not the planned 250 MW total. The campus is part of QTS's Atlanta-area footprint, which spans Atlanta proper, Fayette County, and Gwinnett County.

No certifications, power sources, cooling methods, or confirmed current IT load are published for this campus. The facility type and building codes indicate purpose-built data center construction rather than repurposed industrial space, but cooling architecture, renewable energy commitments, and grid interconnection specifics are not disclosed. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends entirely on when and whether the planned 250 MW reaches operation, a figure that remains a development plan, not deployed reality.
